question: A coronary plaque that causes 70% luminal stenosis on angiography is more likely to rupture and cause acute MI than a plaque causing only 30% stenosis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is actually false. Counterintuitively, smaller but vulnerable plaques (thin fibrous cap, large lipid-rich core) rupture more often than large, stable fibrous plaques. This is why angiographic stenosis does not predict future MI site.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this is false. Plaque vulnerability (thin fibrous cap, large lipid core, macrophage infiltration) determines rupture risk, not size. Most MIs arise from rupture of haemodynamically non-significant (<50%) plaques.
